evidence_source: Attended session command results, retained scratch reports, and operator confirmations

notes: The first unprivileged NAS restore passed content verification but failed ownership: 17 nodes recorded as 0:0 were restored as 1000:1000.

A fresh sudo restore preserved numeric ownership. The original workstation-restore.py eventually wrote its report after completing metadata and symlink-target checks; interruption of chat monitoring did not establish that the process had stopped.
Manual KDBX success was confirmed by the operator and restored to the report after the original helper overwrote that flag.
The unprivileged restore passed content verification but failed ownership. A privileged follow-up used NAS snapshot metadata to repair mismatched numeric owners only within B2 scratch.

A subsequent validator read the actual B2 snapshot and passed file type/size, ownership, modes, mtimes, and symlink-presence assertions. Its final report write failed because the earlier repair report was root-owned; the report was then finalized manually with the B2 snapshot ID.
The temporary validator checked symlink presence, not target strings, and did not test xattrs. Earlier claims that the complete B2 metadata gate had passed were too broad.
The scratch report's elapsed_seconds value of 36.23899483680725 came from the NAS-based repair pass and is not the B2 validation or total restore duration. It is deliberately not reused here.
No repository credentials, file contents, or private keys are included in this record.
